title: Spanish Fort by streetcar; the Southern Syncopators' Gulf Coast hotel jobs
summary: Hirsch recalls riding the train to Spanish Fort as a boy and then his Southern Syncopators five-piece band at the Tivoli Hotel and Wayside Inn, with pay and room and board.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: You mentioned that before. Toe KT, that was out of Spanish Fort.
Johnny Barstorfer. I got a book out there with all of this crap in it. Yeah.
Yeah, but it wouldn't be like you're having gone there.

Well, I was young for that. Believe me, I was young. That was when my daddy was playing out at Spanish Fort. In fact, we used to go out there. I used to go out there with him in the afternoon around one or two o'clock. And then my mother and my sister would catch the streetcar. Streetcar, there were no automobiles in those days. You'd catch, there was a train that used to start at Rampart and Canal. You'd go all the way up. I don't remember. Go out and go out West End Boulevard. You'd cut around and go right down to Spanish Fort. You used to have these stuff

coaches on the back. They'd have like an open air coach. And they'd have about two or three coaches on a streetcar. So if they'd have a big crowd, they'd be able to move them along. Because there was no two-way. There was no two-way. They had to go to the end of the line and come back and start over again. There was only one deal on that. I'm reading a book right now about New Orleans. I mean, I got in this buddy Stahl wrote it. It's very interesting. I'm reading right now about the epidemic of yellow fever when the city almost got wiped out. But it was really something. Did you play across the lake when you were young? Yes. I played at a hotel over there. I played with the southern... No, I played with two bands over there. The southern syncopators was five pieces. We played the hotel. We used to get $15 a week in the hotel for playing dinner and lunch and dinner. About an hour each session. And with that, we got to eat dinner and lunch. they fed us. They fed us. And then we played at another place called Wayside Inn, which was on West Beach, which I don't remember. I've looked for it a thousand times, but it's no longer there. They must have tore it down or something, built something on top of it. And nobody seems to know where Westside Beach is. There was the Wayside Inn, and we used to get $20 a week there playing there from 9 till 12 and 9 till 1 o'clock. And we slept there. So we got about $35 a week in money and free board and free room. Which was the hotel? The Tivoli. Which town was this now? Neluxy. Neluxy, the Tivoli Hotel. The Tivoli Hotel. This, I don't know, I don't think it's there. I don't think it's there anymore.
